My dog ​​has been going to this vet since he was two months old. He's nine now. Every time I go, I spend at least €160 to €240. I used to see Dr. McCarthy, an experienced vet, but now it's other people, the same age as him, charging the same prices. Well, my dog ​​is bleeding from the neck because he really needs his medication, and I walked four miles to get there after calling, and the young man at reception simply informed me that he wasn't going to give him the medication because they hadn't seen the dog for a few months. The reason I'm posting this is because there are other options. There's the animal welfare association on Avenue de la République, which is completely free: all they ask for is a donation. They don't try to empty your wallet or tell you incredibly disgusting lies.

There is nothing worse than a veterinary clinic that profits financially from innocent animals and their loving owners. Shame on you, Dr. McCarthy!

I arrived from the United States with a lot of paperwork, but the veterinarian—who speaks perfect English—was incredibly welcoming and wonderful with my cat despite my stress, and she handled all the formalities with ease. We are very grateful to Dr. Marie Balanger and highly recommend this clinic to everyone.
Exceptionally kind and supportive, but also knowledgeable and diligent. I highly recommend them.
Excellent service. Charming receptionist & very sympathetic Doctor that clearly cares for his patients & animals. English speaking.

Dr. Maccarthy is an excellent and highly regarded veterinarian in the 5th arrondissement. I've entrusted my cats to him for over 25 years, and I can't thank him enough for all the wonderful care he provides them 🙏😍 …
They issued me an EU passport I paid for it then they never registered it in the country system.  Now I’m stuck and can’t travel with my pet as the pet passport is not valid.
Dr. McCarthy has been treating my cats for years. Thank you to him for his skill, his gentleness with animals, and his advice. I highly recommend him.
Thank you Ms. Lejarre for your opinion.

Excellent veterinarian. Dr. McCarthy is very competent, attentive, and always available. My Labrador received excellent care. I recommend him without hesitation.

Thank you again for your invaluable help.

The reception team is also very friendly and reliable, which makes every visit a pleasant experience.

My wife and I are shocked by the death of our little guinea pig at the Saint-Germain veterinary clinic.

Our little companion was returned to my wife in a state of convulsions, in a desperate condition. When we dropped him off around 6:10 pm, the veterinarian explained that the clinic did not offer overnight care and that it would be best to take our guinea pig to another clinic in the 12th arrondissement by 6:30 pm. This clinic offered overnight care (at least a 20-minute drive, not counting the potential delays during rush hour, and the animal was ultimately found to be in agony).
Our guinea pig collapsed before we left the clinic and then suffered a fatal cardiac arrest. Thankfully, my wife wasn't in the taxi. Until now, we had been very happy with the services and care provided by this clinic. We feel the situation deteriorated, that the otherwise very kind staff realized the problem too late, and that at the most critical moment, we were told to manage on our own with our pet and seek treatment elsewhere. This is absolutely unacceptable and not normal.
Needless to say, we now strongly advise against this clinic for guinea pigs in light of this appalling experience. We have requested the surgical report, anesthesia records, post-operative monitoring records, medications administered, and clinical notes to shed light on the sudden decline in our pet's condition.
Indeed, given the conditions of handover, we don't know how our little pet's pain was managed between the operation (morning) and the time of recovery (6 p.m.). We know that guinea pigs are fragile animals and that any surgery is risky, especially with age. We would have fully accepted euthanasia to end their suffering. Furthermore, we question the risk/benefit ratio of the surgery presented during the pre-operative consultation. We meant well by removing a sarcoma from the ear of our little companion, who was otherwise in excellent health, and we lost him. We regret having him operated on because he could potentially have lived a few more months with the sarcoma. We took his life when he was lively, energetic, and full of life.
Ultimately, it was a complete failure, objectively our responsibility due to our choice of this clinic. We should have gone to another facility more focused on animal welfare and offering continuous care.

Update June 2025: We're back in Paris! This time Aussie(our pup) decided heat rashes were the latest fashion trend. Dr. Agathe once again proved why she's the best - immediately diagnosed the issue, prescribed the perfect medication, provided clear printed instructions (because let's face it, we'd forget otherwise), and still had treats ready for our spoiled pup. Her patience with our endless questions and thorough explanations made everything so much easier.

Two visits, two different issues, same excellent service. I highly recommend this clinic and be sure to ask for Dr. Agathe - she's basically a dog whisperer with a medical degree!

===================================================
Dr. Mensior Agathe, a highly skilled veterinarian, provided exceptional care when we urgently needed a fit-to-fly certificate for our pet. Despite our last-minute request, the clinic was able to accommodate us with a same-day appointment.

Dr. Agathe was incredibly patient, friendly, and communicated effectively in English.

She meticulously ensured that all necessary details about our pet were accurately documented on the certificate.

Dr. Agathe conducted a thorough examination of our dog, handling them with care and even offering treats to help them feel at ease.

I highly recommend this clinic and be sure to ask for Dr. Agathe.

Absolutely excellent, especially after having visited many vets in Paris. She truly strives to diagnose problems, minimize expenses, is very gentle with the animal, and is very dedicated and accommodating to owners. She has a real mastery of procedures and handling techniques (the only vet who knows how to draw blood without causing pain!). In short, perfect (Dr. Mensior).
Thank you, Madam, for your opinion.

I recently lost my dog Trixie to cancer, and I cannot thank Dr. McCarthy and his wonderful staff enough for their care and compassion during this heartbreaking time. Dr. McCarthy served as Trixie’s general practitioner, and he was incredibly kind, responsive, and thoughtful in his approach to Trixie’s end-of-life care. He never pressured us into any decisions. Instead, he truly listened to our concerns and helped us make the best choices for Trixie with empathy and understanding. Through every step of Trixie’s illness, he treated our girl with gentle dignity and genuine love, right up until the very end.

The entire staff at Dr. McCarthy’s clinic was just as compassionate and supportive. From the front desk to the vet techs, everyone showed us kindness and patience. Their support made an incredibly difficult time a little bit easier. Though our hearts are heavy with sorrow, we feel immense gratitude that Trixie’s final days were filled with such gentle care. My family will forever be grateful to Dr. McCarthy and everyone on his team for helping us give Trixie the peaceful, dignified farewell she deserved.

Fantastic clinic! I've tried many in the area and I must say I'm very satisfied with the entire team. The veterinary assistants are incredibly friendly, attentive, and efficient. I also want to express my sincere gratitude to Dr. Mensior, who is as kind as he is competent, and who knew how to put my very fearful dog at ease by taking all the time he needed. So, a huge thank you! It's so nice and important to feel confident when our animals have problems (mine has a lot...), and they don't give the impression of just chasing profits either. I highly recommend them!

I want to share my experience so you don't make the same mistake I did by entrusting your pet to this clinic. My dog ​​was sick, and he wasn't a typical patient. I took him in, and in hindsight, I realize they weren't at all interested in finding out what was wrong with him. Furthermore, Dr. McCarthy admitted he'd made a mistake by not ordering the necessary tests (ultrasound and X-rays) from the start. These tests were only done a month after his first visit, on the day he died. He didn't show much interest in him, and I was even given a bill and a cat's analysis. Being a good professional also means knowing when to step back if you're not feeling your best for whatever reason, especially when you work in a field like yours with living beings in your care. Furthermore, with his 30 years of experience, he was the only one who felt my dog ​​was getting better; for them, it's normal for a dog to lose 500 grams in a day. I even received a completely inappropriate comment from the vet, McCartney: "You have a phone," as if he were more interested in neighborhood gossip than his work. They tell you they'll keep you informed, but not at all; they don't speak clearly, to the point that they know your dog is dying, and they send you to another clinic, giving you false hope. They're like robots with learned behaviors, more so than humans. So, give yourself every chance to find a vet who truly wants to care for your companion and tries to understand what's wrong with him in order to give you all the possible options. My partner and I will be happy to know that this story doesn't repeat itself; that's the reason for this summary.
Dr. MacCarthy is excellent and surrounded by a great team. Competent and kind.
